A1.justification: Both readable PDFs describe the same Lens study, with closely matching main sections, equations, and experiments. v1 ends after the references despite referring to an appendix; v2 supplies Appendices A-F. The supplied content supports reliable comparison, while newly supplied details do not establish that existing experiments were changed or rerun.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-classification experiments, sensor-control comparisons, latency analyses, and quality-estimator ablations in Tables 1-3 and Figures 3-8, using its collected ImageNet-ES Diverse dataset.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds segmentation and detection examples, an entropy ablation, label-wise analyses, and further experimental results in its appendices.

M1.justification: The classification algorithm, maximum-softmax VisiT score, and three CSAs remain unchanged. Appendix A.1.1 and Table 4 introduce task-specific adaptations: VisiT averages confidence over highlighted dog pixels for segmentation or valid bounding boxes for detection. These are limited procedural extensions.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates classification, whereas v2 also evaluates semantic segmentation and object detection through dog-focused qualitative examples using FCN, DeepLabV3, Faster R-CNN, and SSDLite300 (Figures 9-10). These introduce substantially different output requirements on the existing Luminous and Diverse imagery. Dynamic scenes and other proposed applications remain future work.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds entropy as an evaluated alternative to confidence-based VisiT across the generalizability models. The original sensor-control, oracle, DG, TTA, and four OOD-scoring comparator sets remain. Appendix E.2's mention of MSP does not establish a separate newly evaluated comparator in the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: Table 4 introduces a qualitative protocol for the additional tasks, including dog-focused segmentation, a detection confidence threshold above 0.6, and source-image and AE comparisons. Existing classification protocols are largely retained. Appendix E.4.1 additionally describes TENT as updating all model parameters, conflicting with the retained BN-layer description; this changes the reported setting but does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds confidence-versus-entropy ablation results (Table 5), accuracy analysis conditioned on source-domain label performance (Figure 11), segmentation/detection case studies (Figures 9-10), and a DeiT confidence-correctness diagnostic (Figure 15). Table 13 also supplies the full ResNet18 candidate-count sensitivity analysis. Table 14 principally tabulates the EfficientNet analysis already shown in Figure 6.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five random seeds for the CSA analysis in Section 5.2. v2 adds no repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or explicit changes to uncertainty estimation. Figure 11's boxplots describe variation across labels rather than uncertainty from experimental repetitions.

E6.justification: v2 adds entropy scores, label-wise findings, task-specific qualitative outputs, and additional candidate-count results. Table 5 reports near parity between confidence and entropy, with average accuracies of 85.6 versus 85.5 on Luminous and 59.8 versus 59.9 on Diverse. Existing Table 1 values also change, including EfficientNet-B0's Luminous Lens accuracy from 80.9 to 81.2. Section 5.1 corrects the stated Luminous advantage over Oracle-F from 47.58% to 29.1%, consistent with 78.6 minus 49.5.

T1.justification: The sensor-selection optimization and classification confidence definition in Section 3 remain unchanged. The appendices add procedural descriptions and conceptual explanations, without new formal assumptions, theoretical results, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The principal contributions and claims about Lens, VisiT, CSAs, ImageNet-ES Diverse, accuracy benefits, capture latency, and compensation for model-size differences remain. The added phrase 'test-time input adaptation' names the existing approach, while embodied AI is an additional prospective application rather than a new demonstrated core claim.

C2.justification: Appendix A substantially expands v1's brief limitations discussion with task-specific scoring requirements, missing advanced-task annotations, hardware-dependent performance, rapid-scene latency constraints, and unevaluated radial distortion and representation-learning uses. Appendix B adds interpretations of label-wise behavior and confidence versus entropy. Its assertion that entropy does not exceed confidence is overly broad relative to the small entropy wins in Table 5.

D1.justification: Appendices C and E supply previously unavailable hardware specifications, banner printing and alignment instructions, ROI cropping procedures, dataset partitions, model-weight sources, classifier fine-tuning details, and optimizer, learning-rate, batch-size, and epoch settings. These chiefly document existing work. Some details remain inconsistent, including E.1's 10,000 validation reference samples versus 1,000 in Tables 9 and 11. The advertised code and dataset URL is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography are unchanged. Works discussed in the added appendix were already listed in v1, and the central positioning relative to model adaptation, domain generalization, and prior sensor-control research remains the same.

P1.justification: The shared main text retains its section order and is largely unchanged. v2 corrects author-header text, adds 'test-time input adaptation' terminology, resolves the undefined appendix references, and organizes supplementary material into Appendices A-F. These changes do not amount to a substantial rewrite of the shared narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 9-16 and Tables 4-14, substantially expanding the visual documentation with task-output grids, label-wise boxplots, testbed photographs, banner and scene-control diagrams, and detailed setup and result tables. Some displays elaborate existing material, particularly Table 14's presentation of Figure 6 results. The original figures and main table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 remedies an important completeness and reproducibility deficiency: v1 repeatedly refers to an absent appendix, while v2 supplies detailed collection and experimental procedures alongside additional diagnostic evidence. The entropy ablation and label-wise analysis strengthen scrutiny of VisiT, and the Oracle-F gain correction improves numerical accuracy. The new task evidence remains qualitative, and inconsistencies in validation counts, TENT settings, and the entropy interpretation limit precision, but the overall gain in documentation and assessable evidence is substantial.
